**The test DB is now protected against the leftover data.** The listing perf test deletes earlier runs' fixtures in `beforeAll` (the S3-F3 pattern), so a killed or crashed run no longer leaves 200,000 rows that slow every later suite.

## Exit criteria (PLAN §16)

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 10k listings with photos processed < 1 h on staging | ⛔ **not runnable (H3); projected FAIL at current sizing** | Measured locally: one media process (8-core dev machine, pool of 10 jobs, `IMAGE_SLOTS = 2`, sharp using every core). Feed-size photos (1600×1200 JPEG): **4.6/s ≈ 16,400/h**. 12 MP camera photos: **2.2/s ≈ 7,900/h**. PLAN §4.1 has ~30 media per listing (60M for 2M listings), so 10k listings ≈ 300k photos ≈ **18 h** for one process at feed size. Processing is CPU-bound (≈ 1.75 core-seconds per feed photo), so < 1 h needs ~20 such processes (≈ 150+ cores at burst). The pipeline scales out (stateless media containers, per-tenant fair share), but the deploy runs one media container |

## Reviews

All three ran on `git diff sprint-S2-done..f777e92`. Every finding below was checked against the code before acting on it.

### security-auditor: 2 must fix (fixed in S3-F10)
- **PARTNER members could open seller documents.** `media.documents.read` reused `listing.read`, which every role has, so a PARTNER member could list and open a listing's nota simple or contract (seller name and DNI). Now it needs a listing role (`listing.create`). Test `[S3-F10]` (PARTNER and unknown roles refused).
- **API uploads could run the API out of memory.** The per-user cap on buffered uploads (S3-F8) existed only in the web relay. A token holder calling the API directly could send many 20 MB bodies at once (2.4 GB at the rate limit). `createUploadSlots` moved to `platform/rate-limit` with a per-process total (8 × 20 MB). The API route takes a slot in `onRequest`, after the session and before the body is read, and releases it when the response finishes or the connection closes; the web relay uses the same caps. Tests: `[S3-F10]` 429 before the body is read and the slot freed after, plus the unit test for the process total.
- **Medium/Low → S4-F1:**
  - the network-shared `properties` row carries owner-only `external_ref`, quality score and freshness columns;
  - bookmarks are member-private only in app code, not in RLS;
  - `check`/`register` trust any stored hash, and the media list shows `sha256` to other agencies (an existence probe, and attaching without the file);
  - signed upload URLs are not tied to a listing or a byte quota;
  - impersonating staff may upload and delete documents.
- Confirmed sound: the S3-F4/F7/F8/F9 least-privilege fixes hold; video links are never fetched (provider id only, embed rebuilt server-side); images are magic-byte, size- and pixel-capped, re-encoded with metadata dropped, and re-hashed in the worker; Client Mode strips commission, private fields, quality and tags server-side.

### code-reviewer: 2 must fix (fixed in S3-F10)
- **A listing could have images and no cover.** `ensureCover` ran only when a file became a floor plan. A listing uploaded with floor plans only, then one turned into an image, kept no cover. It now runs on any kind change. Test `[S3-F10]`.
- **Media edits emitted no outbox event** (golden rule 6). Kind, cover, alt text, room type, order and video links changed without an event, so the stored quality score (photo count) went stale, and S7 read models would miss them. New `media.listing.changed` is emitted in the same transaction by every media edit and recomputes the quality score. Test `[S3-F10]` counts one event per edit.
- **Should fix, done now (cheap):**
  - listing content reads ran two queries at once on one transaction (refused in pg 9): now one after the other;
  - the document purge's continuation trigger stopped changing at the 64-character cap, so BullMQ dropped the next job: now a counted `-c<n>` suffix (test `[S3-F10]`, 5,000 continuations all distinct);
  - the S3-F6 EXPLAIN check now carries its tag.
- **→ S4-F3:** `failStaleBulks` fails QUEUED actions behind a busy pool; no listing purge job exists (soft-deleted listings and their documents stay forever); DOCUMENT rows removed by migration 0056 left refcounts unscheduled; raw-`Tx` cross-module functions need a PATTERNS decision. **→ S4-F1:** the impersonation delete exception.

### perf-auditor: FAIL → fixed in S3-F10
- **Filtered list queries matching few rows broke the 20 ms SQL budget at 5,000 listings:** `status=ACTIVE` sorted by updated 19–32 ms, status + price_desc 16–32 ms, the reference prefix 17–42 ms. The cost grew linearly with agency size.
- **Root cause (found while fixing):** a plain status index would not have helped. Under RLS the planner only uses leakproof conditions as index conditions; the test DB confirms `enum_eq`, `textlike` and `upper` are **not** leakproof (`int2eq`, `texteq`, `text_ge` and `text_lt` are). The fix, migration 0058:
  - stored `status_code smallint` (`LISTING_STATUS_CODES`, `not null`, so a new enum value without a code fails loudly);
  - stored `ref_key = upper(ref)`, filtered as a C-collated byte range `>= P and < succ(P)`;
  - `properties_agency_status_idx` (partial, live rows), `properties_agency_ref_key_idx`, and the missing `properties_agency_country_idx` (auditor should-fix).
- **The perf test missed the case** (every seeded listing was DRAFT). It now seeds 88 % draft / 10 % active / 2 % sold, adds list scenarios for a rare status under each sort and a prefix that matches nothing, and EXPLAINs them. Measured by `[S3-07] [S3-F6] [S3-F10]` on 200,000 listings, as `app_user` under RLS:

  | Statement | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Rare status, newest | 17–32 ms | **0.23 ms** |
  | Rare status, updated | 19–32 ms | **0.43 ms** |
  | Rare status, price_desc | 16–32 ms | **0.39 ms** |
  | Reference prefix (1,000 matches) | 17–42 ms | **2.4 ms** |
  | Reference prefix, no match | — | **0.15 ms** |
  | Country, no match | walks the agency | **0.13 ms** |

  The unfiltered sorts and subtree filters are unchanged (0.1–0.5 ms). List p95 over all scenarios stays < 300 ms, each scenario ≤ 10 queries.
- Within budget: dashboard API (member context + `listOwn` + one batched tags read), feed-api (Cache-Control + ETag/304 unchanged), workers (250-listing chunks, batched writes, SKIP LOCKED sweeps, image slots, pixel caps), and dashboard routes (listings/[id] 232.8 KB, listings 223.1 KB, bookmarks 179.5 KB, all ≤ 250 KB; unchanged on a fresh build).
- **→ S4-F2:**
  - bulk actions queue quality recomputes for fields the score never reads;
  - zod ships to the listings client (17 KB headroom on the editor route);
  - the media RSS test assumes the compiled worker's idle size;
  - `properties` now has 22 indexes (non-HOT updates): review before S6;
  - the 0050/0051/0057 indexes are not `CONCURRENTLY` (fine pre-launch; add a migration check);
  - `perf:smoke` is still a stub.

## Demo script for Shahzaib

Local stack. The dev database needs migrations 0045–0058 and the latest RLS. Every seeded login uses the password **`Inmolink-demo-2026`**.

1. `pnpm infra:up`, then `pnpm db:migrate && pnpm db:rls && pnpm db:seed`, then `pnpm db:seed:scale --agencies=3` (a Spain-sized taxonomy and listings), then `pnpm dev`. Open <http://localhost:3100>.
2. Log in as **`admin@costa-homes.demo.inmolink.test`** and open **Listings → New**. Pick a type and a city, then save: you land in the editor. Fill basics, drop the map pin and set precision to approximate. Add specs, features, a price and the commission. Watch the autosave indicator. Add an English and a Spanish translation; note the origin badges. Lock a field.
3. Open the **Media** section. Drag in 10 photos (one HEIC if you have an iPhone photo): each is hashed in the browser and uploaded in parallel with progress. Drag the same photos in again: they are skipped instantly (already stored, zero bytes sent). Reorder by dragging, set a cover, mark one as a floor plan, and give one a room type and alt text.
4. Add a YouTube link under videos: it sits in the order with the photos. Upload a PDF under documents and open it (a signed download). Try a JPEG renamed `.pdf`: it is refused.
5. Look at the **quality score** and its fix-it hints. Add a longer description and the missing translation, and the score rises within seconds (the worker recomputes on each change).
6. Open **Listings**. Filter by status, by a region (its whole subtree) and by the start of a reference. Sort by price and switch the columns. Save the view. Select several listings and run a bulk action (status → Active, or price +5 %): a progress bar follows the worker job.
7. Bookmark two listings into a folder with a note and open **Bookmarks**.
8. Log in as a scale-seed agent of another agency (`a1-u1@s1.scale.inmolink.test`): shared listings show without commission, owner contacts or internal notes, and **documents are not available** to anyone outside the owner agency (nor to PARTNER members of it).

## Risks and decisions needing approval

- **Exit criterion and media capacity (decision).** At one media container the criterion is about 18× off. Options:
  - (a) size media for burst: scale media containers on demand during imports (a media worker host pool, e.g. 2–3 × 64-core hosts for the < 1 h target), possibly with a cheaper first pass (thumb/small first, larger variants later);
  - (b) restate the criterion as a per-core rate plus a scaling target (e.g. "≥ 15k feed photos per hour per 8 cores, linear with containers"), with the 1 h figure for a defined staging size.

  I recommend (b) now, and (a) planned with S6 imports. Please choose; until then the criterion stays open.
- **S3-10 moved to S4** (after S4-02): it needs development and unit targets. Please confirm.
- **Deploy notes.** Migration 0058 adds two stored generated columns to `properties` (a table rewrite) and three indexes, without `CONCURRENTLY`. It is fine before production data. Run `pnpm db:migrate && pnpm db:rls` locally. The dev database also needs 0053–0057 if not applied.
- **Local test DB hygiene.** The shared test DB keeps every run's rows, so a killed run can leave large fixtures (233k listings this time). The listing perf test now cleans its own. Others follow the S3-F3 pattern.
- **Human steps still open:** H3 for S3-F7/S3-F9 (R2 bucket `inmolink-media-work`, the media token and Redis ACL secret), H1 (legacy dump: S2-06), H3/H4/H5 for S0-15, and the deploy prerequisites under STATUS → Handover.
